> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ea61f4fc5f98ea19f95fab6b0eb1cfb37536ebaf && git checkout ea61f4fc5f98ea19f95fab6b0eb1cfb37536ebaf
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 529ed7d9391bcb47ea859bfe9ae4b0d1766fc234 75dcf734c357ea2305e4123bbddbf19e01e8724a && git checkout -B drift-repro 529ed7d9391bcb47ea859bfe9ae4b0d1766fc234 && git merge --no-ff 75dcf734c357ea2305e4123bbddbf19e01e8724a

```

</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a

> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 529ed7d9391bcb47ea859bfe9ae4b0d1766fc234` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `93b0b1196366f9d9fda4becdb6e1e7926ba8f202`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/engine-execution-plumbing.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/script-runner.ts

Read: card #33786 (body and all six comments, the os-dev-report 6897591859 included), #33694 (body; the owner's ruling on cloud#3826 is read as that body quotes it, cloud#3826 itself was not an input), ADR-0090 D10 rule 4 with its 2026-09-16 and 2026-09-20 notes, ADR-0151 D5, PR #34018 (body, 13 files, net diff against merge base `0ac112fc`). The remaining eight files (tests, regenerated `content/docs/**`, the changeset, the cli pin) are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Check-runs on this head at review time. Completed, success: Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, the three `Lint · scoped` jobs, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs, Auto Label, filter, both shard planners. No check-run has failed. This record's verdict is the contract's; it does not stand in for those conclusions.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `ExecutionContext.performedBy` gains optional `agentId`, `conversationId`, `confirmationId`. Accept-set widening. Right. Because the object strips unknown keys, a host that already put `agentId` there had it dropped on `main` and now has it carried to hooks; that is the intended effect and the changeset says it.
2. `clientId` required to optional, with `.refine(requiredOneOf(['clientId', 'agentId']))`. It is BOTH, on two different faces:
   - Accept set (what parses): a pure widening. Every value that parsed on `main` parses to the same output; `{ agentId }` newly parses; `{}`, `{ conversationId }` and `{ confirmationId }` are refused before and after. Nothing is newly refused, so no `(narrowing)` arm is owed.
   - Reader guarantee (what a consumer of a parsed context may assume): narrowed. `ExecutionContext['performedBy']['clientId']` goes from `string` to `string | undefined`, and the published schema's `required: [clientId]` becomes an `anyOf`. A strict TypeScript reader outside the repo that dereferences `performedBy.clientId` as a string stops compiling.
   - The declaration lines: `Clause-②: yes` with the word "widened" is right for the accept set, and the changeset body states the reader-side loss in its "What to do" paragraph with the one-line fix. That is sufficient under the repo's definition of the arm (the arm is read off the accept set). The PR body's 「只放宽」 is true of the accept set only; the next clause of the same sentence corrects it. Right.
   - First-party readers, read in the tree: `runtime/src/action-execution.ts#apiForwardAgentOf`, `mcp/src/tool-call-interceptor.ts`, the three plugin-audit writers and `plugin-auth` all guard `clientId` with a `typeof` or `nonEmpty` check, and each also requires `principalKind === 'agent'` or a string `clientId` before acting. An `{ agentId }` context makes none of them treat the caller as an OAuth agent. Right.
3. The refusal of a performer-less `performedBy` changes shape: on `main` an `invalid_type` issue at `performedBy.clientId`, now a custom issue at `performedBy`. Still a refusal; a consumer matching on the old path or code is the only thing that moves. Not declared; harmless (N3).
4. `HookContext.provenance` gains optional `performedByAgentId`, `performedByConversationId`, `performedByConfirmationId`. Widening of what a hook may read. Right.
5. `ScriptContext.provenance` (exported interface of `@objectstack/runtime`) gains the same three optional members. Widening. Right.
6. The claim that the published JSON Schema carries the rule as `allOf: [{ anyOf: [...] }]` and that `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` does not grow is not visible in the diff (the regenerated `.mdx` shows four optional keys and no rule) and was not probed. `requiredOneOf` is on the projectable list in `packages/spec/src/shared/refinement-projection.ts` and the baseline file is not in the diff, which is consistent with the claim; Test Core and the generated-artifact gates, in progress, are what confirm it.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/33786-in-product-ai-performed-by.md`: `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime` at `patch`. Those are exactly the three released packages whose `src` the diff moves; `packages/cli` moves a test only. Right.
- `Clause-②: yes` on both the PR body and the changeset. Right: a published schema's accept set moves.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` on both. Right by the definition of record ("the change to what a metadata author can WRITE"): `ExecutionContext` is assembled by the server and `HookContext.provenance` is stamped by the engine; a metadata author writes neither, and no authorable key, value or type is added. `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Shape, optional siblings (A) or a discriminated union (B): A is accepted. B would add a discriminant, which is the new actor vocabulary the ruling refuses, and would break every `performedBy?.clientId` reader on the other arm. The cost of A is that the schema admits combinations no producer builds, `{ clientId, agentId }` and `{ clientId, conversationId }`; see N1.
- Key names: `agentId` / `conversationId` / `confirmationId` accepted over `agentName` / `pendingId`. `agentId` and `conversationId` are the `ToolExecutionContext` names for the same values. `confirmationId` is right and `pendingId` would be wrong: the key names a decided confirmation and must cover both confirmation seams in `packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts`, whose ids are spelled differently (`proposePendingAction` returns `id`, `IActionConfirmationService.submit` returns `pendingId`). See N2 for what that costs.
- Hook-side names: the flattened `performedBy` + key prefix accepted; it is the existing `performedByClientId` convention and a nested object would be a second shape for one mark.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` versus `added` on the #31740 precedent: answered `none`, see ②. The precedent was not re-read (not an input); if the seat holds hook-READABLE members to be protocol, that is a reading of the definition for the seat to rule, and it would flip the line and the spec level together. Not escalated: the text of record says "write".
- Widened file surface (objectql `buildProvenance`, the two sandbox files, the cli pin): accepted, and necessary. Without the `buildProvenance` copy the three hook keys would be declared and never populated (ADR-0049), and the cli pin enumerates the body face. The round-2 claim 6897603637 already names these files. No write reaches `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/**` or `docs/adr/**`.
- Item (b), the ruling: the owner's ruling as #33694 carries it ("Accept AI-on-behalf, conversation id and confirmation id on the write context, using the existing `performed_by` / `on_behalf_of` columns plus contract fields. Do not add a new actor vocabulary") covers a second producer of `performedBy` on the write context. ADR-0151 D5 does not refuse it: D5 refuses `performedBy` for a performer that IS the subject, and here the subject is the person. The dev's no-stop is right.
- ESCALATED to the seat (bookkeeping, not a finding on this head): the tree's ADR text now disagrees with the spec. ADR-0090 D10 rule 4 says a caller of any kind other than an agent principal "records the principal it authenticates as, and the missing `performed_by` is itself the record that the principal acted for itself"; ADR-0151 lists "the meaning of `ExecutionContext.performedBy` (the OAuth client that acted for a person)" under Leaves unchanged; the 2026-09-20 note calls it a one-key object. The dev report says the ADR note is "Noted, not filed". The carrier card on the skills lane should exist before this merges, naming all three passages, so the disagreement is tracked and not merely remembered.
- No `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**`; no `security` label is owed by that rule.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts`

- Against the ruling: holds. The existing pair is used, no actor vocabulary is added, `actor` does not move, `userId` stays the person, and `onBehalfOf` is deliberately NOT set on the in-product path. That last choice is what keeps attribution out of authorization: `onBehalfOf` is the key the confused-deputy intersection reads, so setting it would have made this an authorization input.
- Against ADR-0151 D5's three reasons: reason 1 (the row would say the agent acted for itself) does not arise, `on_behalf_of` is the person; reason 2 (one key, two id namespaces) is honoured on the envelope by separate `clientId` and `agentId` keys; reason 3 (delegated model) does not arise, the person is the subject on their own grants.
- Never an authorization input: checked in the tree. No reader of `performedBy` outside the audit writers and the forward-credential mint exists, and the mint requires `principalKind === 'agent'`, an `oauthScopes` array and a string `clientId`. `assemble-execution-context.ts` still emits `{ clientId }` or `undefined` and nothing else, so no door in this repository can be made to emit `agentId` from a request.
- S1 (should-fix) — the "server-constructed" sentence does not hold against the values the same docblock equates the keys to. The docblock says "No request header, body member or model output may set any key of it", and in the same breath defines `agentId` as "the same value as `ToolExecutionContext.agentId`" and `conversationId` as "the same id as `ToolExecutionContext.conversationId`". `ToolExecutionContext.agentId` is documented in `ai-service.ts` as "the `:agentName` from `/api/v1/ai/agents/:agentName/chat`", and a conversation id reaches the tool loop from the caller that continues a thread. Read literally the sentence forbids the first producer's only sources; read loosely it admits a caller-named id onto an envelope whose own ADR note (2026-09-20) refused `traceId` and `requestId` for being caller-controlled. The contract has to say which: state the producer's obligation, that a key may carry an id a request named only after the server resolved it in its own store for the person in `userId` (the agent it actually ran, a conversation that person owns, a pending item that person's approval decided for this operation), and that an unresolved id is not stamped. Without it the audit answer #33694 exists to give, "AI changed this for this person in this conversation", can name a conversation the person never had. Prose only: the docblock and the `.describe` strings, plus the regenerated reference.
- N1 (nit) — the schema admits `{ clientId, agentId }` and `{ clientId, conversationId }`, while the prose says each key is "set only by its own producer". Server-constructed, so nothing reaches it; left as an accepted deviation of shape A.
- N2 (nit) — `confirmationId` is one key over two stores (the in-app pending action id and the pending-confirmation service item id), the pattern the docblock avoids for the performer. Which store an id resolves in follows from the performer key beside it; #33694 should say so when it records the id. Follow-up on #33694, no change here.
- N3 (nit) — the performer-less refusal now reports at path `performedBy` with a custom code. Accepted.

`packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`

- The docblock's count (five marks), the copy rule ("each key is copied from its `ExecutionContext.performedBy` sibling") and "never an authorization input" agree with `buildProvenance` and with the audit writer's rule of reading `provenance`, never `session`.
- S2 (should-fix) — the published description states an audit behaviour the tree does not have, and pre-decides the mapping #33694 owns. `performedByAgentId`'s `.describe` says "the audit writer records it in `sys_audit_log.metadata` as `performed_by` beside `on_behalf_of`", and the `ExecutionContext.performedBy` describe says the same of all four keys. At this head `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts` (~:2117 and ~:2270) reads `provenance.performedByClientId` and nothing else, so an in-product AI write produces a row identical to the person's own; the changeset says so ("a separate change to the audit writer") and the description contradicts it. It also commits the writer to putting the agent id in the `performed_by` key that holds `sys_oauth_application` ids today, which is ADR-0151 D5 reason 2 and which this PR's own body tells #33694 not to do. Reword both descriptions to what is true on this head: the key is carried for the audit writer, which records it under #33694, without naming the column as fact.
- The `performedByClientId` description is untouched and still true.

`packages/objectql/src/engine-execution-plumbing.ts` — agrees. `buildProvenance` copies each of the three keys from its `performedBy` sibling and from nothing else, coerces with `String`, drops empty values, and keeps returning `undefined` when no mark survives, so a write with no origin still carries no `provenance`. `buildSession` is untouched, so the performer never reaches `session`; the new engine test asserts exactly that.

`packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts` — agrees. The three marks are projected member by member through `declaredStringMarks`, from the engine's `buildProvenance` output and never from the payload, as the comment above the block requires.

`packages/runtime/src/sandbox/script-runner.ts` — agrees. The `ScriptContext.provenance` type lists the same seven members the body runner projects and the spec declares.

Tried and not broken: an `{ agentId }` context reaching the forward-credential mint (refused by the `principalKind` and `clientId` guards); a hook or body writing provenance back (not a path this diff opens); `{ agentId: '' }` (parses, and `buildProvenance` drops it, the same class as an empty `clientId` on `main`).

Open on this head: S1, S2. No must-fix. Both fixes are prose in the two `hits` files and their regenerated references; each moves the head and earns a delta review.
